Common Progressions: i-PVI-PVI: Hiv: Ev; Hb >It: PV

Aeolian outlines the basic structure of a minor seventh chord (root, > 3rd, 5th, b7th) and these extensions: Sth, 11th, and 13th.

Pattams for Aeolian (Roots are circled; notes in parentheses are the >6th degrees.)

Fig. 19

Aeolian is the modal name for the natural minor scale, and it is the mode that ail other minor modes are compared to. It is the sixth mode of the major scale and corresponds to the vi chord in major keys. Butits main role is to service the i chord in minor key progressions.

Common descriptions of the Aeolian mode inciude “romantic,” “heavy,” and “melodramatic"-small wonder it is such a favorite among hard-rock guitarists. Fig. 20 makes good use of the 6th degree of D Aeolian in a D minor rock ballad example,
